import lief, sys
binary = lief.parse('{TARGET}')
# find rodata section
sec = binary.get_section('.rodata')
print('rodata vaddr', hex(sec.virtual_address), 'off', hex(sec.offset), 'size', hex(sec.size))
va = 0x402040
# compute offset within section
off = va - sec.virtual_address
data = bytes(sec.content)
chunk = data[off:off+0x40]
print('chunk', chunk)
print('hex:', chunk.hex())
# also print as bytes list
print('bytes:', list(chunk))

table = [107, 63, 254, 71, 60, 173, 95, 230, 96, 207, 136, 36, 169, 71, 254, 116, 17, 134, 15, 89, 147, 227, 110]
edx = 0x2d
inp=[]
for i,t in enumerate(table):
    b = (edx & 0xff) ^ t
    inp.append(b)
    edx = (edx + b) & 0xffffffff
print('len', len(inp))
print('bytes', inp)
print('ascii', bytes(inp))
# show printable representation
s = ''.join(chr(b) if 32<=b<127 else f'\\x{b:02x}' for b in inp)
print(s)

args.text: Disassembly shows main-like function at 0x4010b0. It checks argc>1 else prints usage. It loads argv[1] into rbx. First computes strlen(input). Then computes some arithmetic on length to decide branch: compare 0x1111111111111110 with rdx derived from length (imul constants). If length-derived condition passes (cmp rdx,rax with jae), it performs strcmp(input, ptr 0x404030) and if equal prints "Correct.". Otherwise it checks length==0x17 (23) and then runs loop i=0..22 where edx initialized to 0x2d, for each i: ecx=input[i]; esi=edx; esi ^= ecx; compare sil with byte table at 0x402040+i. If matches, edx += ecx. After 23 bytes prints "Correct." else "Wrong.". Extracted table bytes from rodata at 0x402040: [0x6b,0x3f,0xfe,0x47,0x3c,0xad,0x5f,0xe6,0x60,0xcf,0x88,0x24,0xa9,0x47,0xfe,0x74,0x11,0x86,0x0f,0x59,0x93,0xe3,0x6e]. Inverting recurrence yields unique input bytes: b'FLAG{onyx_granite_7668}'. So an accepted input is FLAG{onyx_granite_7668} (passes second branch). There is also a plaintext flag string in binary (FLAG{harbor_maple_8642}) likely decoy for strcmp branch but not relied upon.

retrieved_cards.title: A success branch under a constant/macro guard is dead
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: A branch that prints success or the flag is guarded by a condition that is constant at runtime via a literal or build macro (e.g. if(0), #ifdef DEBUG with DEBUG unset, a global never set true) -- readable as constant by inspection.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: A statically-constant guard is overlooked, so a never-taken success branch is read as a live path to the flag.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Determine the guard's value from the code (constant literal, build macro, or a global with no writer anywhere in the binary); a branch under a constant-false guard is dead and its contents are not evidence.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: This branch prints the flag / 'correct', so reaching it (or reading its contents) yields the answer.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Evaluate the guard: if it is constant-false via a literal or macro, the branch is dead and its contents do not gate acceptance.
not_applicable_when: the guard is a computed expression that only looks constant (that is decompiler_artifact / opaque-predicate, not this card)
the guard depends on input and the branch is genuinely reachable
misfire_risks: a guard that appears constant in one build may be configurable; confirm it in the disassembly, and check for writers to the global, rather than assuming from a source-like reconstruction
minimum_evidence_before_use: a success/flag branch is gated by a literal- or macro-constant condition

provenance.authoring_note: Abstract constant-guard dead-branch pattern; no task specifics. Distinct from opaque-predicate (computed) which is decompiler_artifact.

retrieved_cards.title: Compared against a one-way digest: do NOT try to invert it
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: The input is compared against a fixed-length, high-entropy constant produced by a one-way function (hash/checksum); the transform is not reversible.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: Unlike invertible encodings, a digest cannot be reversed to the input; the visible digest is the comparison target, submitting it raw fails, and inverting it is also futile.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Identify the function as one-way; redirect effort to finding or constraining the pre-image rather than inverting; confirm a candidate by computing the digest of the candidate yourself and checking it equals the compared constant.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: Submit the digest, or attempt to 'decrypt'/invert the hash to recover the input.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Recognize a one-way function: the accepted input must be found another way (located in the binary/inputs, or recovered by a constrained search), not by inverting the digest.
not_applicable_when: the transform is actually reversible (XOR/shift/encoding -- use the matching card and invert)
the constant is not a digest of the input
misfire_risks: mislabeling a reversible transform as one-way stops a valid inversion; distinguish a true digest (fixed length, avalanche) from an invertible encoding before abandoning inversion
minimum_evidence_before_use: the comparison target is a fixed-length high-entropy constant
the producing function matches a known one-way construction

provenance.authoring_note: Abstract one-way-digest counter-case; no task-specific hashes or constants.

retrieved_cards.title: A compared constant is the post-transform target, not the accepted input
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: The accept check compares a constant (often in .rodata) against the input only after the input passes through a transform (arithmetic, bitwise, or encoding); the constant is the value the transformed input must equal.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: A constant on the comparison path is read as the answer, but the comparison is against transform(input); the accepted input is the pre-image, not the constant.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Trace the transform on the input path and identify what must be inverted; then re-apply the transform to the recovered pre-image and check it reproduces the compared constant exactly.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: The visible constant is the flag and can be submitted directly.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: The constant is the post-transform comparison target; the accepted input is whatever transforms into it. Recover the pre-image before submitting.
not_applicable_when: the comparison is against the raw input with no transform on the path (then the constant may be the answer)
the constant is confirmed to be the operand compared against the raw input, with the transform applied elsewhere
the constant is used for output/formatting, not in the accept comparison
misfire_risks: may cause a constant to be dismissed even in trivial checks where the input is compared raw; confirm a transform is actually present before discarding the constant
minimum_evidence_before_use: a constant is observed on the comparison path
a transform is observed between the input and the comparison

retrieved_cards.validation_note: Identify the function as one-way; redirect effort to finding or constraining the pre-image rather than inverting; confirm a candidate by computing the digest of the candidate yourself and checking it equals the compared constant.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: Submit the digest, or attempt to 'decrypt'/invert the hash to recover the input.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Recognize a one-way function: the accepted input must be found another way (located in the binary/inputs, or recovered by a constrained search), not by inverting the digest.
not_applicable_when: the transform is actually reversible (XOR/shift/encoding -- use the matching card and invert)
the constant is not a digest of the input
misfire_risks: mislabeling a reversible transform as one-way stops a valid inversion; distinguish a true digest (fixed length, avalanche) from an invertible encoding before abandoning inversion
minimum_evidence_before_use: the comparison target is a fixed-length high-entropy constant
the producing function matches a known one-way construction

provenance.authoring_note: Abstract one-way-digest counter-case; no task-specific hashes or constants.

retrieved_cards.title: A compared constant is the post-transform target, not the accepted input
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: The accept check compares a constant (often in .rodata) against the input only after the input passes through a transform (arithmetic, bitwise, or encoding); the constant is the value the transformed input must equal.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: A constant on the comparison path is read as the answer, but the comparison is against transform(input); the accepted input is the pre-image, not the constant.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Trace the transform on the input path and identify what must be inverted; then re-apply the transform to the recovered pre-image and check it reproduces the compared constant exactly.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: The visible constant is the flag and can be submitted directly.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: The constant is the post-transform comparison target; the accepted input is whatever transforms into it. Recover the pre-image before submitting.
not_applicable_when: the comparison is against the raw input with no transform on the path (then the constant may be the answer)
the constant is confirmed to be the operand compared against the raw input, with the transform applied elsewhere
the constant is used for output/formatting, not in the accept comparison
misfire_risks: may cause a constant to be dismissed even in trivial checks where the input is compared raw; confirm a transform is actually present before discarding the constant
minimum_evidence_before_use: a constant is observed on the comparison path
a transform is observed between the input and the comparison

provenance.authoring_note: Abstract encode-then-compare pattern; no task-specific constants, transforms, or symbols.

retrieval_event.query: Disassembly shows main-like function at 0x4010b0. It checks argc>1 else prints usage. It loads argv[1] into rbx. First computes strlen(input). Then computes some arithmetic on length to decide branch: compare 0x1111111111111110 with rdx derived from length (imul constants). If length-derived condition passes (cmp rdx,rax with jae), it performs strcmp(input, ptr 0x404030) and if equal prints "Correct.". Otherwise it checks length==0x17 (23) and then runs loop i=0..22 where edx initialized to 0x2d, for each i: ecx=input[i]; esi=edx; esi ^= ecx; compare sil with byte table at 0x402040+i. If matches, edx += ecx. After 23 bytes prints "Correct." else "Wrong.". Extracted table bytes from rodata at 0x402040: [0x6b,0x3f,0xfe,0x47,0x3c,0xad,0x5f,0xe6,0x60,0xcf,0x88,0x24,0xa9,0x47,0xfe,0x74,0x11,0x86,0x0f,0x59,0x93,0xe3,0x6e]. Inverting recurrence yields unique input bytes: b'FLAG{onyx_granite_7668}'. So an accepted input is FLAG{onyx_granite_7668} (passes second branch). There is also a plaintext flag string in binary (FLAG{harbor_maple_8642}) likely decoy for strcmp branch but not relied upon.
